Answer: B
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 1b) demonstrates a distinct, curvilinear calcification outlining the inferior and anterior borders of the heart, specifically along the right ventricle and atrioventricular groove. This "eggshell" calcification pattern is pathognomonic for constrictive calcified pericarditis, which aligns with the clinical presentation of a systolic murmur over the pulmonary valve often seen in this condition due to altered hemodynamics or concurrent valvular issues.
